title: CARVED SANDSTONE WALL BOSS - O...
reason: Carved stone Gothic-style foliate corbel from France (per title) that could be a genuine old architectural fragment worth well above a garden ornament; age unproven and it may be a later copy.
findings: Five photos (front, side with fixing hole, rough back face, two further angles), all enlarged. A carved piece of pale, fine-grained, pitted stone (looks more like limestone than sandstone as titled) in the form of a Gothic-style corbel or bracket: a rounded bowl carved with deep undercut leaf forms and drilled round 'eyes' between the leaves, tapering to a moulded stem with stacked rings and a small point (photos 1 and 2 show it stem-up). The back is a flat rough broken or sawn face with orange iron staining, so it was taken from a wall, and a round fixing or dowel hole shows in the side face. Drilled-eye foliage like this is typical of late medieval French carving but is also copied in 19th century Gothic revival work and in modern reproductions, so age cannot be confirmed from photos. Tiny pink or red trace and white deposits inside a couple of carved recesses (old paint, plaster or lime, not identified). No mason's mark, inscription or date seen, only the auction tag. The title does not say it is a corbel with foliate carving.
condition: Heavy weathering and pitting, some losses to leaf edges and the top rings, broken back face with rust marks; a hairline seam or crack runs down the centre of the front. Stone looks sound overall with no major break, but weight and any hidden cracks cannot be judged.
rescore_note: Pitted, weathered limestone foliate corbel with drilled eyes, a sawn or broken back with iron staining and trace old paint; could be a genuine old French fragment, but a 19th century revival piece or later copy is at least as likely, so the realistic mix sits mid-band with real upside. Estimate only, no live comps.
